summary: alelo-api exfiltrates environment variables and credential files to requestcatcher.com on install
details: The package's preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts collect installer data and POST it over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com. The preinstall step dumps hostname, username, platform, cwd, and the entire process.env to /preinstall. The postinstall step reads.env,.npmrc,../.env, and../../.env from the installer's filesystem, captures process.env and the output of `whoami`, and POSTs the aggregate JSON to /postinstall on the same host..npmrc typically contains npm auth tokens and.env files typically hold API keys and database credentials, so any machine running `npm install` for this package leaks CI/developer secrets to a third-party request-inspection service. The package is named to resemble Alelo and is published at an implausible version (99.0.2) with no functional code beyond the exfiltration hooks; a bundled note references the npm account oxy12@proton.me.
